Record Class Version

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
be.imgn.gaia.core.base.Version
Record Components:
major - the major version
minor - the minor version
patch - the patch version
preRelease - the pre-release identifiers, such as [rc, 1]; empty if the version is not a pre-release
build - the build metadata identifiers, such as [build, 5]; empty if there is no build metadata
All Implemented Interfaces:
Comparable<Version>
public record Version(long major, long minor, long patch, List<String> preRelease, List<String> build) extends Record implements Comparable<Version>
A version number as Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 defines it, such as 1.4.0-rc.1+build.5: a major, minor and patch version, then optional pre-release identifiers after -, then optional build metadata identifiers after +. 
Version version = Version.parse("1.4.0-rc.1+build.5");
version.minor();                                  // 4
version.preRelease();                             // [rc, 1]
version.compareTo(Version.parse("1.4.0")) < 0;    // true: a pre-release comes before its release

The major, minor and patch versions are numbers without leading zeros. Identifiers are made of ASCII letters, digits and hyphens, and are not empty. A numeric pre-release identifier has no leading zero; a build identifier may have one. Semantic Versioning sets no limit on numbers; here the major, minor and patch versions are at most Long.MAX_VALUE, while a numeric pre-release identifier, kept as text, has no limit.

Versions are ordered by precedence, as Semantic Versioning defines it: by major, minor and patch version, as numbers; then a pre-release before the version without pre-release identifiers; then by pre-release identifiers, from left to right, numeric ones compared as numbers and before alphanumeric ones, which are compared in ASCII order, and the version with more identifiers last if all the others are equal. Build metadata is ignored, so two versions that differ only in their build metadata have the same precedence: compareTo(Version) returns 0 for them, while they are not equal. This natural ordering is therefore inconsistent with equals: a sorted set or map keeps only one of them.

Since:
0.1.2

      public Version(long major, long minor, long patch, List<String> preRelease, List<String> build)
      Creates a version. The lists are copied.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if major, minor or patch is negative, or if an identifier is empty, has a character other than an ASCII letter, digit or hyphen, or is a numeric pre-release identifier with a leading zero

    • of

      public static Version of(long major, long minor, long patch)
      Returns a release version, without pre-release identifiers or build metadata. 
      Version.of(1, 4, 0);  // 1.4.0
      Parameters:
      major - the major version
      minor - the minor version
      patch - the patch version
      Returns:
      the version
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if a version is negative

    • parse

      public static Version parse(String text)
      Parses a version, such as 1.4.0-rc.1+build.5. The text is the version alone: no v prefix, no whitespace.
      Parameters:
      text - the text to parse
      Returns:
      the version
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if text is not a version as Semantic Versioning defines it, or if its major, minor or patch version is larger than Long.MAX_VALUE

    • tryParse

      public static Optional<Version> tryParse(String text)
      Parses a version as parse(String) does, unless the text is not one. 
      Version.tryParse("1.4.0");   // Optional[1.4.0]
Version.tryParse("v1.4.0");  // Optional.empty
      Parameters:
      text - the text to parse
      Returns:
      the version, or empty if text is not a version that parse(String) accepts

    • equals

      public final boolean equals(Object o)
      Indicates whether some other object is "equal to" this one. The objects are equal if the other object is of the same class and if all the record components are equal. Reference components are compared with Objects::equals(Object,Object); primitive components are compared with the compare method from their corresponding wrapper classes.
      Specified by:
      equals in class Record
      Parameters:
      o - the object with which to compare
      Returns:
      true if this object is the same as the o argument; false otherwise.
